title: A 'validation' observation does not prove a test passed
trigger: When citing a host 'validation' observation as evidence that tests passed, or reading observation counts as a success rate
behavior_delta: Do not cite a 'validation' observation as proof of a pass without reading its raw_preview: reject it as evidence when the preview shows failure markers (fail 1+, not ok, ✖, AssertionError) or when the command only read a test file. Run the tests without a pipe instead when a pass must be shown.
what: Do not cite a 'validation' observation as proof of a pass without reading its raw_preview: reject it as evidence when the preview shows failure markers (fail 1+, not ok, ✖, AssertionError) or when the command only read a test file. Run the tests without a pipe instead when a pass must be shown.
why: observationFromTool (src/hooks/observe.js) marks any Claude Code Bash call whose command contains a word like test or check and whose PostToolUse reports interrupted:false as 'Validation passed'. A piped test run exits with the pipe's last status, and a grep or sed over a *.test.js file matches the regex, so on 2026-09-24 failing runs and plain file reads were recorded as passes.

revisit_when.description: Retire this once observationFromTool stops recording piped runs and file reads as validations (TODO.md item 4).

archived_reason: observationFromTool now records a validation only when a test, lint or type-check runner is a statement's own program, not piped and followed only by &&, and when the output reports no failures. Piped runs and commands that only read test files are no longer validations.
